official_measurement_examples.name: Current ground guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Environment Agency ground-discharge general-binding-rules guidance was updated 23 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ground threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: The general-binding-rules route for discharge to ground normally applies at 2 cubic metres per day or less, subject to all other rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surface threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: The general-binding-rules route for discharge to surface water normally applies at 5 cubic metres per day or less, subject to all other rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: Other permissions
official_measurement_examples.fact: Meeting general binding rules can remove the environmental-permit requirement but does not replace planning permission or building-regulations approval where required.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ1 restriction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A qualifying ground discharge cannot use the general-binding-rules route in groundwater Source Protection Zone 1.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected sites
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected-site and ancient-woodland proximity can prevent use of the general-binding-rules route for a new ground discharge.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public sewer proximity
official_measurement_examples.fact: For newer ground discharges, reasonable connection to a nearby public foul sewer can affect whether the general-binding-rules route is available.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: GBR or permit status does not establish land rights, planning permission, building-regulations compliance or final development yield.

core_rules: GBR compliance is not planning permission
GBR compliance is not building-regulations approval
permit exemption is conditional not blanket
ground and surface-water discharge rules remain distinct
2m3/day and 5m3/day thresholds must not be interchanged
SPZ1 restriction applies to ground-discharge route
domestic sewage scope must be retained
non-standard discharge systems can fall outside GBR
existing and new discharge dates matter
permit status does not establish drainage-field land rights
discharge approval does not establish development yield
no permit record is not proof of lawful exempt discharge
no parcel sewage-discharge clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, GOV.UK, Defra, National Data Library and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. 23 July 2026 ground-guidance update and current thresholds/site/sewer/permission distinctions retained; no parcel promotion.
